pins.definition: A device used to talk to other people over a distance.
A device used for talking to someone who is in another place.
A device used for calling people and sending messages.

situation: A man at a tidy wooden desk picks up an old rotary dial device to make a call.
subject: the telephone
brief: A heavy black Bakelite rotary telephone sits centered on a polished mahogany desk, caught under a bright pool of desk lamp light. A man's hand reaches in from the edge of the frame to lift the receiver from its cradle, while the brass dial catches a gleam. The background is simple and warm, keeping all focus entirely on the device.
prompt: A heavy black Bakelite rotary telephone sits centered on a polished mahogany desk, caught under a bright pool of desk lamp light. A man's hand reaches in from the edge of the frame to lift the receiver from its cradle, while the brass dial catches a gleam. The background is simple and warm, keeping all focus entirely on the device. a 1970s science-fiction paperback cover, airbrushed gradients, a muted offset-print palette with visible halftone, dramatic scale and a confident optimistic mood. It renders an ordinary modern scene as though it were the future someone once imagined, so it suits machinery, travel, work and plans as readily as spacecraft. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
